Senses.PreferredTarget: at the gate of light and shadow
Senses.Note: One spatially loaded idiom covers the sampled uses. Warnings, criticisms, and Hongzhi's qualified acceptance are different appraisals of the same light-and-shadow threshold, not different things. The corpus's own gate/inside-house and formed-image/not-yet-formed-image contrasts establish the definition without requiring an added reading.

Occurrences.Kwic: 如今人未認得光影門頭戶底麤淺底事，將作屋裏事又爭得？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Imperially Selected Recorded Sayings (御選語錄), Yunju Daoying section. Yunju Daoying is the exact speaker who calls this the coarse and shallow business at the gate of light and shadow and contrasts it with the matter inside the house.

Occurrences.Kwic: 惟認光影門頭當作自己。汾陽禪師亦云：『五位參尋切要知，纖毫纔動即差違。』
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Xueguan (雪關禪師語錄): responding to Hengru's request for instruction, Xueguan Zhiyin says that students with coarse activity-consciousness and clouded eyes recognize only the gate of light and shadow as themselves, then quotes Fenyang Shanzhao on the five positions.

Occurrences.Kwic: 光影門頭休駐足，色聲叢裡好撐睛。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Fushi (浮石禪師語錄): in his verse replying to the layman Shen Shuding, Fushi Tongxian says not to halt at the gate of light and shadow and to open the eyes amid the thicket of forms and sounds.

Occurrences.Kwic: 雖然如是。光影門頭了事底漢即得。祇如賓主未分。影像未具時。如何履踐。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Extensive Record of Chan Master Hongzhi (宏智禪師廣錄), in Hongzhi Zhengjue's hall discourse: Hongzhi Zhengjue allows a person who settles the matter at the light-and-shadow gate, then asks how one proceeds before guest and host divide and before an image is formed.

SearchAliases: at the gate of light and shadow
Zen at the gate of light and shadow
Senses.Explanation: The gate of light and shadow is the records' visible threshold contrasted with the matter inside the house: people mistake its coarse, shallow business for what is within (光影門頭戶底麤淺底事，將作屋裏事). Elsewhere Xueguan Zhiyin says students "recognize only the gate of light and shadow as themselves" (惟認光影門頭當作自己). The phrase also enters verse as a place not to stop: "do not halt your steps at the gate of light and shadow" (光影門頭休駐足). Hongzhi supplies a notable counter-deployment: "a person who settles the matter at the gate of light and shadow will do" (光影門頭了事底漢即得), then immediately asks how one proceeds before guest and host divide and before an image is formed. Zen thus bends ordinary light, shadow, and doorway language into a recurring label for the visible or reflected threshold that records contrast with the inside of the house, oneself, and the not-yet-formed image.
